call.x: Apply for funding to strengthen conservation and heritage science infrastructure by building sustainable capability, improving access to nationally significant facilities and driving innovation with industry partners. You must be based at a UK research organisation eligible for AHRC funding.
n: Run by Arts and Humanities Research Council (AHRC). The organiser sets the rules; Eligible Calls reads this call from UKRI Funding Finder (ukri.org).

UKRI-unlocking-advanced-capabilities-in-.heading: How we will assess your application

blocks.text: Assessment process
We will assess your application using the following process.
Applications to the Unlocking Advanced Capabilities in Conservation and Heritage Science funding opportunity will be assessed by a panel.
Panel

For applications, the panel will review and rank fundable applications in order of priority for funding. As this funding will expand the established Research Infrastructure for Conservation and Heritage Science (RICHeS) distributed infrastructure network, the panel will seek to support a complementary portfolio of projects that:
strengthen and extend the existing RICHeS distributed infrastructure through the addition of new or enhanced capabilities
address clearly evidenced user needs and unmet demand, while expanding access to nationally significant facilities, expertise and resources

achieve an appropriate balance across geographical regions, heritage science disciplines and technological capability areas, avoiding unnecessary duplication of existing infrastructure, capability or established techniques
demonstrate a high level of innovation, including the development, adaptation or novel application of techniques that enhance capability within the heritage science sector
deliver clear benefits and pathways to impact for a broad range of users and stakeholders, including the heritage sector, other scientific disciplines, industry, policymakers and the public

include meaningful collaboration with small and medium-sized enterprise (SME)s and other partners, or are delivered through a consortium that brings together the expertise required to achieve the project’s objectives
demonstrate a credible approach to long-term sustainability, access and legacy beyond the period of UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) funding
AHRC reserve the right to use the panel recommendations to create a balanced portfolio of applications and will make the final funding decisions.

These portfolio considerations will be applied alongside the assessment of individual applications to ensure that the final portfolio maximises the overall strategic impact and capability of the RICHeS network.
For more information on how we prioritise applications for funding please visit How we make decisions .
Principles of assessment
We support the San Francisco declaration on research assessment and recognise the relationship between research assessment and research integrity.
Find out about the UKRI principles of assessment and decision making .
Using generative artificial intelligence (AI) in expert review

Generative AI may be used only for the purpose of language refinement during application assessment. When using generative AI to refine the language of a review, expert reviewers and panellists must ensure that:
no part of the application being assessed is entered into a generative AI tool
no personal information from the application is disclosed
generative AI is not tasked with understanding, summarising or evaluating the application’s content
Expert reviewers and panellists must also:
comply with relevant intellectual property and data protection legislation
not take into account or speculate within their assessment whether generative AI has been used to develop the application
For more detail see our policy on the use of generative AI .
Assessment areas
The assessment areas we will use are:
strategic contribution to the RICHeS network, including the extent to which the proposed capability strengthens, complements and adds value to the existing distributed infrastructure
innovation and advancement of conservation and heritage science capability, including the development, adoption or novel application of technologies, methods and approaches
access, demand and user benefit, including the extent to which the proposed infrastructure addresses unmet need, expands access and delivers benefits to users and stakeholders
knowledge exchange, impact and wider benefits, including pathways to impact across the heritage sector, other scientific disciplines, industry, policymakers and the public
quality of collaboration and partnership, including the effectiveness of consortium arrangements and engagement with SMEs and other partners
sustainability and legacy, including long-term operational viability, access, resilience and plans beyond the period of UKRI funding
portfolio fit and complementarity, including contribution to a balanced portfolio across geographic regions, disciplines, capabilities and user needs, while avoiding unnecessary duplication
Find details of assessment questions and criteria under the ‘Application questions’ heading in the ‘How to apply’ section.

consortium.quote: Unless otherwise provided for in the specific call/topic conditions, only legal entities forming a consortium are eligible to participate in actions provided that the consortium includes, as beneficiaries, three legal entities independent from each other and each established in a different country as follows: – at least one independent legal entity established in a Member State; and – at least two other independent legal entities, each established in different Member States or Associated Countries.
